summary: We developed OrbitAir, a smart CO₂ monitoring dashboard designed to improve air quality and astronaut safety in space stations. It monitors carbon dioxide levels across different station modules, using colour-coded indicators and alerts to identify unsafe conditions. It also provides smart recommendations, such as activating ventilation, to help address problems. OrbitAir addresses the challenge of maintaining breathable air in enclosed environments. It is important because it helps protect astronauts, supports faster responses, and promotes safer, healthier, and more efficient space missions.
details: OrbitAir is a smart CO₂ monitoring and air-quality management system designed to improve the safety and well-being of astronauts living and working in space stations. It works by monitoring carbon dioxide levels across different station modules, including the laboratory, exercise area, crew quarters, galley, airlock, and node/hub. The dashboard displays real-time simulated readings using colour-coded indicators, where green represents safe levels, yellow indicates moderate levels, and red highlights areas that need attention. It also provides alerts when CO₂ levels become too high and uses AI-assisted recommendations to suggest actions such as activating ventilation. The main benefits of OrbitAir include improving astronaut safety, identifying air-quality problems early, supporting faster decision-making, and making air management more efficient. Its intended impact is to create a healthier and safer environment for astronauts while supporting long-duration space missions. The product uses web development tools, Netlify for website hosting, interactive dashboard features, data visualization, and AI-assisted recommendations. What makes OrbitAir creative is its combination of an interactive space-station map, colour-coded monitoring, automated alerts, and smart suggestions in one centralized platform. During its development, important factors such as astronaut safety, accuracy, reliability, efficiency, ease of use, and clear visual design were considered to ensure the system is practical and easy to understand. Our prototype won Best Idea at Jordan's National Innovation and Robotics Championship 2025.
